approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs from a score-ranked population and fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to every real observation in the current session. At a planning step it compares a Thompson batch with up to thirty-two single substitutions by their expected best observed value across two batches. For each imagined first-batch outcome it greedily chooses a second batch using sixteen joint noisy samples, then values that fixed choice with thirty-two separate samples. Once the first batch is actually measured, it executes that same saved second-batch policy using the real outcomes, saved scale and retained graphs. Fresh graphs still get generated but cannot displace this committed recourse; the final unpaired batch uses the inherited one-batch rule.
approach.novelty: Replace the hard sampled marginal improvement calculation with conditional analytic tail integration in that one future-policy consumer. The original sixteen samples supply the selected prefix, while each remaining candidate’s Gaussian tail is integrated analytically in stable log space. Applying the same function to imagined and real recourse can distinguish candidates after the empirical panel has run out of improving samples. There are no listed same-Parent children. The parallel terminal study uses the same integration principle under a different latent covariance and one-batch horizon; it provides neither inherited capability nor independent replication here.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-59436e1eec8f correctly executes all210 saved noisy-conditional recourses, yet its hard16-row marginal estimator has exactly zero selected gain at879/2100 positions and167/210 second batches make no incumbent improvement. Its independent model utility0.007241473479038255 exceeds realized second-batch gain0.003715006147371181 on this selected stream. Full420-window progress is0.022859629874334365 versus0.02399560213969095 for its code Parent n-201fe3876d7a; mean endpoint0.5405543584646847 is lower by0.017413267390789317. The Parent remains refuted/triggered, not technically failed. This is an exposed finite-panel discrimination bottleneck plus unresolved predictive optimism and fresh-support exclusion; it is not proof of universally miscalibrated GP uncertainty. Own full Search reconstruction is policy/scratch/r0077-03-improve-L01/plan/parent-evidence.json, with each original log/trajectory and hash in the15 task audits. Formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de is a different comparator.

hypothesis: Conditional analytic candidate-tail integration replaces the hard16 future-policy marginal estimator in BOTH first-stage valuation and actual saved recourse. For each outer/actual outcome and selected prefix S, preserve the original joint noisy sample coordinates y_S^(r), r=1..16. Under the inherited conditional Gaussian (mu,V), compute m_jr=mu_j+V_jS V_SS^(-1)(y_S^(r)-mu_S), v_j=V_jj-V_jS V_SS^(-1)V_Sj, and t_r=max(B_A,max y_S^(r)). Rank remaining eligible j by logmeanexp_r log E[(N(m_jr,v_j)-t_r)_+]. Empty S uses scalar analytic EI. Original retained-index order breaks all exact ties, including all exact deterministic zeros, without reselecting unavailable identities. The candidate coordinate is integrated, so the policy may resolve positive model tails absent from the finite hard panel. This is an obstacle intervention on marginal discrimination, not an extension of the refuted saved-commitment prediction; useful transfer requires the full real-window observable to move.

finding_summary.headline: Analytic recourse improved two-batch progress and mean score, with uneven gains
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment supports the registered conditional-tail intervention in this saved-recourse host: numerical discrimination reached actual purchases and the complete real-progress statistic improved. It does not rehabilitate the earlier prediction that commitment alignment alone would help. Stable scalar logEI, finite Gaussian prefix conditioning and the information-respecting future-policy rule all operated as adopted; the finite discrete greedy construction and retained candidate set still limit what can be inferred from those literature principles. The parallel terminal experiment tests the same integration principle under different conditions, so the two are not independent replications or separately additive contributions.

Resolving empirical zeros did not resolve the whole search limitation. The saved model predicted mean second-batch gain of 0.01220112, above the realized 0.00799012, and 135 of 210 second batches still found no new incumbent. At the integrated policy's own prefixes, 1,148 selected candidates still had zero hard-sample marginal despite a finite analytic log gain; a positive tail is not calibrated real benefit. Moreover, total incumbent gain in the 2,175 late purchases fell from 1.33274 to 0.83542, and 3,588 of 4,350 purchases failed to beat their generating parents. Better full-panel transfer therefore does not establish uniformly better late refinement. These observations leave selected-stream predictive optimism and candidate availability as distinct limitations. A better calibrated surrogate or a search policy that explicitly models candidates generated after feedback could address those kinds of limitations, but the 32,765 excluded fresh graphs have unknown outcomes and their benefit is untested.

The molecular audit shows that the search can already build ring-rich aromatic families and cyclic amines. Its remaining proposal limitations include repeated truncation to tiny fragments, chemically questionable attachments and unspecified stereochemistry: products with at most five heavy atoms rose from 84 to 217, and nitrogen-halogen attachments from 463 to 766. More coherent scaffold-preserving and local-environment-aware proposal operators could address that representational weakness. These chemical associations do not explain the intervention's score change or prove a benefit from any unpurchased alternative. The result prices this estimator change within its retained host; it leaves the separate contributions of the GP, graph operators, survivor rule and commitment unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
The conditional-tail calculation executed throughout planning and all 210 real second batches, with every ordered choice reproduced independently. At 687 real recourse positions every available hard-sample marginal was zero; analytic integration distinguished candidates in all 687 and changed the choice at 678. All 210 second-batch sets changed, replacing 1,450 of 2,100 purchases relative to the passive hard policy on the same inputs. First-batch sets changed in 71 of 210 planning decisions. Independent evaluation remained separate from selection, and all 4,350 purchases entered real feedback.

The registered useful-transfer test passed: mean realized progress across all 420 adjacent two-batch windows rose from 0.02285963 to 0.02337166, an increase of 0.00051203. Zero-progress windows fell from 151 to 126. Mean second-batch gain rose from 0.00371501 to 0.00799012, and zero-gain second batches fell from 167 to 135 of 210. Final mean score rose from 0.54055436 to 0.55060773, a code-Parent gain of 0.01005337 that exceeds the separate 0.002 target. The three seed-macro changes were +0.05190155, +0.00319801 and -0.02493945; eight task/seed endpoints improved and seven fell. The paired task-safety check passed against the code Parent. Against the separate formal Anchor, the mean remained lower by 0.05642259 and the task-safety check failed on sitagliptin_mpo. This descendant cannot satisfy the criterion that requires the formal Anchor itself as code Parent.

The extra calculation increased mean announcement time from 1.67 to 3.41 seconds. Every task completed within the frozen timeout; no essential selection fallback or missing outcome was used as successful evidence.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families and cyclic amines, with unresolved stereochemistry, reactive attachments and recurrent small fragments
molecular.overall_character: The complete frozen Search panel was read: all five tasks and seeds 0, 1 and 2, covering all 15 Child/code-Parent trajectory pairs. Each side has 4,350 accepted optimizer products plus the matched initial observations. Every optimizer row joins exactly, by SMILES, score and accepted serial, to its original log feedback. context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; no authorized trajectory or log path is missing. The comparison here is with actual code Parent n-59436e1eec8f. Formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de is a separate comparator and receives no molecular comparison in this report. The Child mainly emits medium-sized aromatic or heteroaromatic scaffolds decorated with carbonyls, imines, ethers, halogens and amines, with fused or spiro saturated rings in some families and very large repeated heteroaromatic assemblies in another. Under identical RDKit perception, 4,110/4,350 products contain rings and 4,060 contain aromatic atoms, versus 4,262 and 4,226 in the code Parent. Child medians are 30 heavy atoms, four rings and three aromatic rings; Parent medians are 31, four and three. These agree qualitatively with the digest ring-closure and aromatic-text counters; those counters measure SMILES presence, not aromatic atom fractions. Ring creation and aliphatic cyclic-amine construction are demonstrated capabilities, not missing capabilities. Plausibility varies within these families. Many constituent motifs are ordinary medicinal chemistry, but N-halogen bonds occur in 766 Child products versus 463 Parent products, O-halogen bonds in 76 versus 124, and peroxide bonds in 91 versus 88. None of either node's accepted optimizer SMILES carries explicit atom or bond stereochemistry; the same RDKit procedure finds at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 1,899 Child products versus 2,355 Parent products, and no assigned centre in either. A reduction in unassigned-centre-bearing structures is not an improvement in stereochemical specification. Small products with at most five heavy atoms increase from 84 to 217; products with at least 50 heavy atoms are 276 versus 269. These are molecule-presence counts on accepted optimizer rows, excluding initials and retaining multiplicity across sessions. They do not count every unpurchased graph generated internally. All counts use the same sanitized-SMILES, SMARTS and stereocentre conventions for both nodes, documented in policy/scratch/r0077-03-improve-L01/molecular/aggregate.json. Synthetic and stability concerns below are structural readings, not measured synthesis yields, toxicity, solution-state speciation or physical binding evidence. Score gradients are associations in purchased molecules; no unpurchased outcomes, mechanism activation, component mediation or causal explanation is inferred. Full provenance and original-source hashes are in policy/scratch/r0077-03-improve-L01/molecular/provenance.json; task-specific original-source/copy, log and audit citations follow each task.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted products are mostly compact, extensively aromatic three-ring molecules: median 25 heavy atoms and three rings, with 835/870 ring-containing and 833/870 aromatic products. The recurring families combine an indole or another fused azaaromatic core with an aryl-linked amide/amidine, methoxy groups and carbon- or nitrogen-bound halogens. Seed 0 favors an N-chloro amidine on a dimethoxy indole; seed 1 ends at a fused azaaromatic N-fluoro carboxamide; seed 2 favors a partly unsaturated fused carbocycle carrying an N-sulfanyl carboxamide, a hydroxymethyl group and a methylamino substituent. The same code Parent had median 25 heavy atoms and three rings. Parent seed bests were principally indole carboxamides with N-brominated attachments, while the Child reaches amidine, azaaromatic and less fully aromatic variants. N-halogen presence is 359 versus 362 and carbonyl presence 547 versus 771; this is a chemistry redistribution rather than disappearance of the attachment liability. Stored best-score pairs, Child versus actual code Parent: seed 0: 0.42570769607214154 versus 0.40497388700123543; seed 1: 0.48211544265448975 versus 0.4163503402962837; seed 2: 0.4597940970593737 versus 0.4484138510190879. liabilities: N-fluoro/N-chloro amides or amidines and terminal N-sulfanyl substituents raise attachment stability and synthesis concerns, even when the graph is accepted.
Tiny halogen/peroxide fragments still appear at the low-score end; peripheral variants share a compact aromatic family rather than establishing broad tractable scaffold coverage.
missing_features: The observed favorable size and aromatic/polar arrangement are present, but the output lacks a consistently chemically ordinary set of alternatives around them: nitrogen-bound halogens and terminal nitrogen-sulfur attachments remain recurrent.
No absent pharmacophore is demonstrated to be required by these scores. Resolved configurations of the minority of stereogenic products are unrepresented, and their score benefit is unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited seed-1 best scores 0.48211544265448975, the seed-0 amidine 0.42570769607214154 and the seed-2 N-sulfanyl amide 0.4597940970593737. In contrast, hydroperoxy fluoride scores 0.0, and the cited large ring-containing bis-heteroaryl aminomethyl product scores 0.00010079397549203362. The latter shows that ring/aromatic presence alone is insufficient: compact placement of the heteroaromatic and polar groups distinguishes the observed favorable family from both tiny fragments and overextended combinations. N-halogen and N-sulfur bonds coexist with favorable scores, so the score does not certify ordinary attachment chemistry. The trajectory does not isolate any single substituent as the cause.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make local-environment-aware substitutions and functional-group edits available so promising scaffolds can also be explored through ordinary carbon-bound halogens and chemically coherent polar attachments. A favorable score with a reactive attachment does not prove that attachment is required or that replacing it improves the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For n-e68846780093 and code Parent n-59436e1eec8f on their complete paired Search panels, explicit atom stereo, explicit bond stereo and assigned tetrahedral-centre counts are all zero under matched conventions. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces asymmetric ring and linker structures without resolving their stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support configuration-preserving and configuration-generating edits where the molecular graph admits stereochemistry, and retain the resulting isomeric identity through ring and linker transformations. Learn any benefit from the same session. The available molecules establish absent specification, not a universal benefit of a particular configuration or a known solution-state stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e68846780093 on all accepted Search products: 217 have at most five heavy atoms, compared with 84 in n-59436e1eec8f; 276 have at least 50, compared with 269. Large structures are not uniformly poor: the same aromatic assembly session purchases a 32-heavy-atom structure at 0.6164626924595342 and a 72-heavy-atom structure at 0.6170343137254902. The stream also reaches 118 heavy atoms. These size conventions are identical for Child and Parent and are descriptive rather than universal cutoffs.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffold truncation and repeated motif growth remain insufficiently controlled relative to the generator's own favorable structural neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide scaffold-preserving contraction, coherent ring/linker replacements and controlled motif growth so search can change connectivity without repeatedly collapsing to tiny fragments or duplicating large assemblies. Use the current session's measured neighborhood to guide size and connectivity; retain access to multiple size regimes because the observed scores do not justify one fixed size limit.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
